Sources include Rust API Guidelines, Performance Book, Rustonomicon, and production codebases like tokio, serde, and axum.

items.name: negotiation
items.author: wondelai
items.description: Prepare for pricing talks, partnership calls, and vendor renewals using Chris Voss-style tactical empathy instead of improvising concessions.
items.summary: Negotiation is an agent skill teaching Chris Voss FBI hostage-negotiation tactics for salary, contract, vendor, and high-stakes conversations. Core principle: people want to feel understood and safe, so empathy and listening beat argument and compromise splitting. The skill scores preparation 0-10 against eight frameworks. Tactical empathy vocalizes the counterpart perspective before stating your position. Mirroring repeats the last one to three critical words with silence to prompt elaboration. Labeling names emotions with It seems like phrasing to diffuse negatives. Calibrated questions use How and What instead of accusatory Why, including How am I supposed to do that for price pushback. Accusation audits preempt negatives early. That is right summaries aim for genuine understanding, distinct from dismissive You are right. Ackerman bargaining sequences offers at 65, 85, 95, and 100 percent of target with precise final numbers plus a non-monetary bonus. Black Swan discovery hunts hidden constraints or motivations. Diagnostics cover BATNA, counterpart styles, and voice delivery including late-night DJ tone after key statements.
highlights: Eight frameworks: tactical empathy, mirroring, labeling, calibrated questions, accusation audit, That's right, Ackerman,
Ackerman method sequences 65-85-95-100 percent offers with precise final numbers and a non-monetary sweetener.
Accusation audit lists negatives the counterpart may think and addresses them before objections surface.
Calibrated How and What questions replace Why to reduce defensiveness during price or scope talks.
0-10 scoring rubric rates preparation against tactical empathy, audits, labels, and Black Swan hunting.

items.description: Let Claude intelligently propose response depth options before generating long or short answers.
items.summary: Token Budget Advisor (TBA) intercepts Claude's response flow before answering, allowing users to select answer depth (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) based on token budget constraints. It estimates input tokens using prose (words × 1.3) or code (chars / 4) heuristics, classifies prompt complexity (simple to complex), applies multiplier ranges (3× - 40×) to estimate full response windows, then presents depth options with token estimates. Users trigger it by mentioning token count, response length, or depth control; shortcut phrases like "TL;DR" or "detailed" skip the menu. Each depth level defines content scope: 25% gives core answer only; 50% adds context and one example; 75% includes alternatives and analysis; 100% covers everything. Accuracy is ~85 - 90% (±15%) using heuristic estimation, not tokenization. Estimates input tokens via prose (×1.3) or code (÷4) heuristics before responding Classifies complexity (simple - complex) and applies 3× - 40× multiplier ranges to predict response windows Presents four depth levels with estimated token counts; users select 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% Supports shortcut triggers ("short", "TL;DR", "detailed")
highlights: Estimates input tokens via prose (×1.3) or code (÷4) heuristics before responding
Classifies complexity (simple - complex) and applies 3× - 40× multiplier ranges to predict response windows
Presents four depth levels with estimated token counts; users select 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100%
Supports shortcut triggers ("short", "TL;DR", "detailed") to skip the menu and respond immediately
Maintains selected depth level silently across subsequent questions in session
